## How they got there
Liverpool reached the final as runners-up after losing to Real Madrid 0-1. Their campaign was defined by a dominant profile, featuring a Points per game average of 3.0 that placed them better than 97% of teams in their group and league phase, alongside Shot accuracy at 59.2%, which beat 97% of peers. They also maintained high control with Possession at 59.5%, outperforming 97% of the season's teams on this metric.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model would have selected Liverpool, ranking them second among all knockout teams and placing them inside its top two predictions. With a calculated probability of 31.7% to reach the final, the system viewed their chances as higher than the base rate of 12.5%. The nearest stage to the model's expectation of 2.23 was the semi-finals. This outlook was driven upward by Attacks per game with a value of 57.5 beating 84% of teams (SHAP contribution 0.44), while Pre-season UEFA club coefficient at 101.0 points, beating 75% of teams, pushed the prediction down most (SHAP contribution -0.07).

## Weak spots
Distance covered per game was recorded at 113.1 km, a figure that beat only 25% of teams in the group and league phase. Fouls committed per game stood at 12.0, which was better than just 38% of their seasonal peers despite being marked as lower is better. Long passes accounted for 13.1% of all passes, a metric that beat only 47% of teams in the group and league phase.
